title: Look Up
description: A street of towers at eye level. Drag upward and you tilt your head back: the lens widens from 70 to 140 degrees and eases from rectilinear to stereographic, so the towers lean in, bend and close into spokes around a summer sky. One 360 capture, projected exactly through r = f k tan(theta / k), developed like daylight negative film.
intent: Summer-film genre spec, idea 1 (Look Up): herb's reference 2, the worm's-eye shot of skyscrapers converging into a cumulus sky, turned into a gesture. Reference: factory/reality/herb-refs/2-wormseye-skyscrapers.png; projection family from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisheye_lens#Mapping_function

sources.author: Andreas Mischok
sources.note: 8K HDR, the street and towers. Its sky is replaced inside the sky matte by the cumulus below; baked to a 2048 sRGB cubemap storing scene light / 1.35. A neighbour's ragged shadow up One Canada Square is relit by cloning its sunlit floors down by whole floors (deshadow.py).

sources.author: Greg Zaal, Jarod Guest
sources.note: 8K HDR, the sky above the towers: shrunk about a pole tilted 40 degrees toward its busy side and laid over a mirrored second pass, so a field of small fair-weather cumulus fills the zenith between the towers with the capture's sun behind them; relit by the street's low warm sun from the right of the resting view (warm sunward domes, skylight-blue folds), open blue regraded to a cobalt ramp that deepens to the zenith at hue 209.
